fact_check.claim: Fall 2024 and later: at least 6 courses totaling a minimum of 18 credits
fact_check.note: Page confirms 6 courses, minimum 18 credits.

fact_check.claim: Courses from at least 3 different groups, including at least 3 credits from Group 7 (RE)
fact_check.note: Confirmed.

fact_check.claim: At least two courses at the 2000 level or higher; page does not say whether 1000-level courses count
fact_check.note: Page states the 2000-level minimum and is silent on 1000-level, as the article says. The opening paragraph's 'only two of them required at the 2000 level or higher' is a slightly odd phrasing of a minimum but not wrong.

fact_check.claim: No more than two Group 6 (CE) courses; CE courses designated by CCGB, no petitions
fact_check.note: Confirmed.

fact_check.claim: A course carrying more than one category (e.g. SSC-AS) counts toward only one; undesignated course takes the categories of its cross-listed course
fact_check.note: Both confirmed.

fact_check.claim: Seven group names (Cultural Analysis, Literature and the Arts, and Social Differences; Historical Analysis; Ethics, Cognition, and Moral Reasoning; Social Science and Global Citizenship; Foreign Languages; Communications in Engineering; Race and Equity)
fact_check.note: Names and numbering match.

fact_check.claim: Group 5 (FL) covers language skills and excludes literature courses
fact_check.note: Category is 'Foreign Languages (not literature courses)'.

fact_check.claim: AP credit / S-U grade treatment is not stated on the Fall 2024 page
fact_check.note: Page does not address AP or S/U, as the article says.

fact_check.claim: The Duffield overview page links a search tool for finding courses by category, and links to policies by entry year
fact_check.note: Page links 'Search for Approved Liberal Studies' (liberal-studies.engineering.cornell.edu) and the three entry-year policies.

fact_check.claim: FAQ: the overview page links to the approved list and the denied list
fact_check.note: The overview page links the search tool and entry-year policies but has no link to /approved or /denied.

fact_check.claim: Duffield students can petition courses not already listed or denied
fact_check.note: Confirmed.

fact_check.claim: The petitions page recommends enrolling in listed courses first
fact_check.note: Page recommends enrolling in courses identified as fulfilling the categories; it does not say 'first'. Minor wording.

fact_check.claim: CALS, A&S, AAP, AEM courses must be under 3 credits; 3+ credits not accepted; A&S foreign language and some graduate courses reviewed case by case
fact_check.note: Confirmed, including the exceptions. Previous fix applied.

fact_check.claim: Human Ecology, Brooks School of Public Policy and Nolan School of Hotel Administration courses not accepted
fact_check.note: Confirmed.

fact_check.claim: Denied courses cannot be petitioned again; no petition deadline stated
fact_check.note: Courses already petitioned and approved or denied are not accepted; no deadline on the page.

fact_check.claim: Approved list at /approved can be browsed 'by group' / by category to find courses fitting each category
fact_check.note: The URL serves an 8-page Excel-generated PDF that WebFetch could not read; the overview page calls it only a search/petition-approved reference. Whether it is organized by group is not established. The by-category tool appears to be liberal-studies.engineering.cornell.edu itself.

fact_check.claim: Denied list at /denied shows refused courses
fact_check.note: URL serves a 2-page PDF (created March 27, 2026) that could not be text-extracted.

fact_check.claim: College Confidential thread 'Credit-Filler Courses' dates from July 2008
fact_check.note: Posts run July 2 to 4, 2008.

fact_check.claim: Brown_man1987: Psych 101 reputedly one of the easiest; recommended DSoc 101 over Soc 101 because its median grade is an A
fact_check.note: Matches ('reputed to being one of the easiest classes around'). Previous fix applied.

fact_check.claim: cuapplecider9: others consider mushroom/fungi and dinosaur classes easy; Space Exploration hard without astronomy background, five papers and a C
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Brown_man1987: many easy-A classes uncurved; many science, math, engineering courses curved to a B or B-
fact_check.note: Matches. Previous fix applied.

fact_check.claim: dewdrop87: median grades would appear on transcripts, for students entering Fall 2008 and later; article has not verified it still applies
fact_check.note: Matches. Previous fix applied.

fact_check.claim: The Sun reported in March 2022 that Engineering limited students to 20 credits per semester (down from 23)
fact_check.note: Published March 31, 2022; 20 credits, down from 23. Dated wording is correct. Previous fix applied.

fact_check.claim: One student told the Sun that with the 18-credit requirement it was hard to fit outside electives
fact_check.note: The student (Fair Shen '25) said the credit cap could keep her from taking an outside elective; she noted her design minor already satisfies the liberal arts requirement. The article does not say the 18-credit requirement made electives hard to fit. This is a misattribution.

beats_top.query: cornell engineering liberal studies easy courses
beats_top.why: The first real result is the official requirements page, which has no difficulty guidance; the actual #1 hit (db.raceface.com) is auto-generated filler. Our page leads with the honest answer, the rules and dated anecdotes, which serves the student better.
changes: Correct the Sun electives claim and the FAQ claim about what the overview page links.
Point students to liberal-studies.engineering.cornell.edu (the search tool) for browsing by category.
